_comment: EXAMPLE profile: a site whose session is an opaque bearer token held in localStorage, sent as an Authorization header, sometimes with a second required header. Copy, rename, edit. Nothing here is specific to any vendor.
name: example-bearer-token
site: Example SaaS with an opaque localStorage token and a private API
capture_hint: Be logged into the site in Chrome. Press F12, open Network, click any request to the site's API, right-click it, choose Copy as cURL (bash), and paste into the capture file below.
_extract_note: Header extraction takes the header verbatim, so it does not matter whether the value is a JWT, an opaque string, or a vendor-specific format. A second header can be captured alongside it when the API requires one (tenant, realm, workspace, and so on).
_wire_note: env-file is REGENERATED from the credential store on every wire, so point `path` at a file this profile owns exclusively. If the destination holds any setting this profile does not own, `wire` refuses rather than overwriting it - have your tool read this file and its own settings file separately.

wire.header_comment: # Regenerated by the grab-cookie Skill. Keep this file out of version control.

_verify_note: expired_exit is for a command that signals a dead credential by exit code rather than by text. Use expired_on instead when the signal is in the output.
_ttl_note: Opaque tokens often have no published lifetime. Leave ttl_days null and let the daily doctor detect expiry by probing.
